title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Comprehensive
author: Michael Chen
content:
Purpose
-------
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard on-call and incident response processes, runbook structure, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation rules, game day exercises, and templates for status-page and customer communications. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders, SREs, and support/CS partners.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated routing, private control plane) and critical backend services that affect availability, latency SLOs, billing, or customer data integrity.

Key definitions
---------------
- Incident severity levels:
  - Sev-1: Complete system outage or critical customer impact (SLO broken for >15 minutes for multiple customers).
  - Sev-2: Significant degradation (e.g., elevated error rate, partial outage affecting multiple customers).
  - Sev-3: Minor degradation or localized impact (single customer or low-severity feature).
- Incident Commander (IC): single person responsible for coordination during the active incident window.
- Pager: PagerDuty for real-time paging; Slack #incidents channel for discussions; Zoom bridge for postmortem call when needed.

SLOs and paging thresholds (examples)
-----------------------------------
- API Availability (global): 99.95% monthly.
- Error rate: API 5xx > 1% for 10 minutes triggers Sev-2 paging; >5% for 5 minutes triggers Sev-1.
- P95 latency: >500ms for 10 minutes triggers Sev-2.
- Missed KV cache hits affecting token cost: tracked as Sev-3 unless causing latency increase.

Incident lifecycle (quick steps)
--------------------------------
1. Detection & Triage
   - PagerDuty or monitoring alert triggers on-call engineer.
   - On-call watches initial alert, validates, and acknowledges within 5 minutes.
2. Classification
   - Determine severity, affected services/customers, and potential blast radius.
3. Notification & Escalation
   - If Sev-1/Sev-2: page IC immediately, create incident Slack channel (#incident-<id>), start Zoom bridge, and notify Eng Leads + Customer Success for affected customers.
4. Mitigation & Recovery
   - Follow runbooks below to mitigate; if no runbook exists, perform safe mitigation and rollback to known-good config.
5. Communication
   - Publish status page entry and customer comms templates (see templates section). Provide updates every 30 minutes for Sev-1 until stable.
6. Post-incident
   - Run retrospective, write postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and publish within 7 days. Track follow-ups in JIRA and assign owners and SLAs.

Runbook structure (required for every production service)
-------------------------------------------------------
Each runbook must follow this template and live in confluence under the service page and in the runbook repo:
- Title and short description
- Owner(s) and Ops contact (PagerDuty schedule, Slack handle, email)
- What is "normal" (SLOs, metrics to watch)
- Common symptoms and corresponding severity classification
- Step-by-step mitigation steps (numbered)
- Safe rollback / fail-open instructions
- Post-incident checklist (logs to collect, debug commands)
- Links: dashboards, run links, runbook source repo, relevant ADRs
- Last tested date and game-day notes

Example runbook excerpt (API gateway high error rate)
-----------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm: query /health and /metrics, check Grafana (error rate, request rate), check upstream model pool capacity.
2) If errors due to model pool OOM, scale up pool / drain node (autoscaler commands: kubectl scale --replicas=...).
3) If errors due to networking (e.g., internal LB 502): fail traffic to next region by updating routing policy (runbook includes CI/CD pipeline command).
4) If unknown: revert recent routing or config rollout (see deployment rollback: release-tool rollback --to <tag>).
5) Collect logs: run log-collect.sh --since 30m and upload to incident bucket.

Escalation matrix
------------------
- On-call engineer (first responder) -> Team lead (10 minutes if not acknowledged or mitigated) -> IC (if severity increases) -> Eng Director (for cross-team or >30m unresolved Sev-1) -> CTO (if >2 hours unresolved Sev-1 or customer data loss).
Contact information should be maintained in the on-call roster document.

On-call rotations and rules
---------------------------
- Primary on-call: 1-week shift (Mon 09:00 UTC — next Mon 09:00 UTC).
- Secondary/backfill: adjacent schedule to take escalations and provide handover support.
- Handoffs: on-call engineers must publish a 15-minute handoff note in Slack and update the on-call rota page with ongoing incidents and outstanding follow-ups.
- Time-off & swaps: use the on-call swap tool (internal UI) and notify the team 48 hours in advance for planned swaps.
- Night/weekend rules: If primary is unavailable for >1 hour, PagerDuty auto-escalates to secondary.

Game days (quarterly)
---------------------
Purpose: validate runbooks, measure MTTR, test cross-team coordination.
Format: 4-hour session with tabletop and live-failure injection.
Runbook testing checklist:
- Runbook exists and is up-to-date (last tested < 90 days).
- Owner available and participates in scenario.
- Observability dashboards and synthetic checks validated.
- Post-game-day report: action items, MTTR metrics, runbook updates.

Postmortem requirements
-----------------------
- Owner: IC or incident lead writes the postmortem.
- Timeline: draft within 72 hours, final publish and action tracking within 7 days.
- Contents (must include):
  - Summary (one-paragraph impact statement)
  - Timeline of events (UTC timestamps)
  - Root cause analysis (5 whys or causal diagram)
  - Immediate mitigations and why they worked/didn't
  - Long-term fixes (with owners and ETA)
  - Severity and customer impact list
  - Lessons learned and follow-up verification plan
  - Link to collected artifacts (logs, traces, recordings)

Postmortem template (short)
---------------------------
Title:
Date:
Authors:
Severity:
Summary: (1 paragraph)
Timeline: (ordered list with timestamps)
Root cause: (concise)
Corrective actions: (table-like bullet list with owner + due date)
Verification plan:

Status page & customer comms templates
-------------------------------------
Use lowercase, clear, and customer-friendly language. Keep internal technical detail in the postmortem and internal comms. Update cadence: Sev-1 every 30 minutes; Sev-2 every 2 hours; Sev-3 at major milestones.

Status page template (short)
- Incident ID: IN-<YYYYMMDD>-<NN>
- Impact: e.g., "Customers may experience errors or high latency for the Redwood API in us-east-1."
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Restored
- Affected services: list
- Updates: timestamped entries (UTC)

Customer email template (initial)
Subject: Redwood API incident affecting [service/region] — [IN-YYYYMMDD-NN]
Body:
Hello,

We're investigating an issue affecting [service/region] that may cause [errors/high latency/consistency issues]. Our engineering team has been paged and is actively working on mitigation. We will provide updates on our status page and via this thread every 30 minutes until resolved.

What you can expect: immediate mitigations are in progress; no action required from you at this time.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

— Redwood Inference Operations

Customer update template (follow-up)
- Timestamp
- What we observed
- What we changed (mitigations)
- Current status and next steps

Resolved message template
Subject: Incident [IN-YYYYMMDD-NN] — Resolved
Body:
Hello,

The incident that affected [service/region] has been resolved as of [time UTC]. Root cause: [short summary]. Impact: [affected customers/requests]. Actions taken: [short list]. We will follow up with a postmortem in the next 7 days.

If you experienced issues beyond the window described above, please contact support@redwood.ai.

Incidence communications cadence (internal)
- Pager trigger -> @oncall Slack ping -> IC joins #incident-<id> -> 1st internal update within 15 minutes for Sev-1 -> regular internal updates aligned to customer comm cadence.

Tools and integrations
----------------------
- PagerDuty: primary paging and escalation.
- Slack: #incidents, private incident channels, #ops-notify for wide notifications.
- Grafana/Prometheus: dashboards and alerts.
- Statuspage (external): scheduled updates and maintenance.
- JIRA: tracking postmortem follow-ups and long-term fixes.

Metrics to track for continuous improvement
------------------------------------------
- MTTA (mean time to acknowledge) target: <5 minutes.
- MTTR (mean time to recover) target: Sev-1 < 60 minutes, Sev-2 < 4 hours.
- Postmortem completion rate: 100% for Sev-1/Sev-2 within 7 days.
- Game-day cadence: one per quarter per major service.

Maintenance and ownership
-------------------------
Service owners must review runbooks annually and after each incident. Runbook owners must record last-tested date and update runbooks post-game-day or post-incident. The on-call rota maintainer (ops admin) is responsible for the schedule and must validate contact info monthly.

Appendix: quick checklist for first responder (copy to mobile)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Acknowledge page (within 5 minutes).
- Post initial note in #incidents: service, symptom, severity, first mitigation attempt.
- If Sev-1: create incident channel and invite IC + CS.
- Collect basic telemetry: top 5 errors, recent deploys, region impact.
- If unsure, escalate after 10 minutes to team lead.

Document history
----------------
- 2024-09-12: Created by Michael Chen.
- 2025-05-10: Added game-day requirements (Ruth Gomez).
- 2026-02-15: Revised SLO thresholds, escalation matrix (Evan Park).

End of document
